messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: KV cache growth + continuous-batching perf cliff in prod-west. Observed: queue depth spike, batch scheduler starvation for short requests, tail latency > 3s for chat/embeddings. Alerting: p95 token latency, 5xx rate rising. (pagerduty: PD-7892)
SRE-Oncall (Maya): acked. I'm on it. collecting logs & will triage hot paths. :eyes:
eng-runtime (Ravi): I'm seeing packer backlog and KV cache working set grew ~3x between 23:10-23:18 UTC. suspects: packer packing policy + recent preload change. logs: `kv_cache.evictions=0`, `packer.enqueue.latency=120ms`
eng-platform (Nora): rolling metrics: node GPU util steady, but single-shard latency high. Could be continuous-batching holding long requests and starving short ones.
support (Diego): multiple customer complaints coming in - three enterprise tenants reported request timeouts. CS notified customers A and B; they're asking for ETA.
prod-ops (Jules): can we quickly reduce max_batch_ms and max_batch_size for the packer on prod-west? That might free short-request latency.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): yes. I'm going to apply a temporary policy: `max_batch_ms=20` `max_batch_size=8` on packer pool `pw-prod-west-1` and enable fast-evict threshold for KV cache at `evict_ratio=0.65`.
eng-runtime (Ravi): recommended: also disable `aggressive_prefetch=true` for affected pools — prefetch seems to be feeding cold keys into cache and causing blowup.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): executing now. `kubectl -n runtime exec deploy/packer-prod-west -- /bin/sh -c "apply-config --pool pw-prod-west-1 --set max_batch_ms=20 max_batch_size=8"`
deploy-bot: deploy started: packer-config-hotfix-2539991234 by Maya. CI checks passed.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): toggled `aggressive_prefetch=false` on the pool. Also triggered KV cache quick-evict: `kvctl evict --ratio 0.65 --pool pw-prod-west-1`
eng-runtime (Ravi): logs show immediate drop in enqueue depth from 1400 -> 420 within 60s. KV cache size trending down.
qa (Sam): running synthetic short-request suite against prod-west canary (10% traffic). will report p50/p95 in 2 mins.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): initial telemetry: p95 token latency dropped from 3.2s -> 620ms at 23:24 UTC. 5xx rate decreased but not to baseline. continuing observation.
support (Diego): customer A reports improved responsiveness. Customer B still seeing occasional timeouts (retrying). Updated CS escalation. Lina will coordinate proactive message if we don't reach full recovery in 30m.
eng-platform (Nora): I see a residual tail: mixed long/short batching still results in some starvation. We should consider a short-request priority queue in the scheduler. filed ENG-INT-412 for follow-up.
eng-runtime (Ravi): agree. Short-term we can enable `pack_priority_short=true` param on the scheduler, but that requires careful rollout. propose canary to 5% after immediate mitigation.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): rolling canary: enabling `pack_priority_short=true` on 5% of packer instances in prod-west. command:```
kubectl -n runtime patch deploy/packer-prod-west --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"pack_priority_short":"true-canary-2539"}}}}}'
```
deploy-bot: patch applied to 5% canary. monitoring latency impact.
eng-runtime (Ravi): canary looks good: short request p95 down 40%, long requests steady. No increase in errors so far.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): promoting canary to 25% now. will watch for contention.
prod-ops (Jules): capturing full customer impact: affected tenants ~0.5% of total traffic but 6 enterprise customers had degraded UX. billing/ingestion unaffected.
support (Diego): creating summary for CS: `incident id PD-7892: transient KV cache blowup + batcher starvation. mitigations applied: reduced max_batch_ms/size, disabled aggressive prefetch, KV quick-evict, enabled short-request prioritization canary. Next steps: monitor, postmortem.`
customer-success (Lina): noted. If we have a 30m window with steady metrics, will send escalation note and offer customer A a credits package if asked.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): metrics look stable for 12 minutes. p95 near baseline, 5xx at 0.02% (pre-incident 0.01%). keeping channel open for 30m before handing off.
eng-runtime (Ravi): will draft a patch to make `aggressive_prefetch` default off for packer pools pending ENG-INT-412. Also include KV cache safeguards: max working set and auto-evict triggers.
eng-platform (Nora): please add tracing hooks to trace short vs long packing paths for next deploy. helps root-cause.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): handoff timeline: I'll stay for 30m then hand to night oncall. If stable at 23:55 UTC, closing page.
qa (Sam): synthetic suite shows steady-state 15m p95=580ms for short requests, long p95 unchanged. passing.
support (Diego): CS note prepared, awaiting final OK from Maya.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): OK to send. final runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-batch-regression. Follow-up: ENG-INT-412 and ENG-OPS-729 tracking long-term fixes.
customer-success (Lina): sending customer note now.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): PD ticket updated and incident set to mitigated. leaving channel in 28m for oncall handoff. :white_check_mark:
eng-runtime (Ravi): quick future action items: 1) rate-limit prefetch per tenant, 2) implement short-request priority queue, 3) add eviction watermark alarms.
prod-ops (Jules): documenting timeline & commands executed in post-incident doc. Will hand over to morning shift for follow-up tasks.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): handing off to night SRE (Victor) at 00:25 UTC. Victor, please monitor p95 and 5xx for next 6 hours and escalate if deviation > 20% from baseline.
eng-platform (Nora): +1 on the handoff. logging all config changes for audit.
SRE-Oncall (Maya): final: thanks all. great quick coordination.
_note: This thread captures an incident triage, live mitigation steps (config changes, evict, canary), customer impact assessment and on-call handoff. Messages are in chronological order and use Slack-style short exchanges, inline code, commands, and bot messages.
